title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and understand directions, use buses, rickshaws and taxis, and give instructions politely or informally.
intro:
Getting around Sindh means rickshaws, minibuses ('coaches'), the occasional train and lots of asking the way. Sindhis give directions generously — usually with landmarks rather than street names: 'go straight, turn left at the mosque, it's next to the bank'.

This unit teaches the **imperative** at three levels of politeness (وڃ / وڃو / وڃجو) and the postpositions of movement: **ڏانهن** 'towards', **کان** 'from', **تائين** 'as far as'.

vocab.note: m. رستو ٻڌائيندا؟ = could you tell me the way?
ساڄي پاسي = to the right (masculine oblique, agreeing with پاسو 'side').
f. Also ريل گاڏي rela gāɗī.
f. e.g. the shrines at Bhit Shah and Sehwan.
هتي روڪيو = stop here (to a driver).

vocab.en: to get off; to go down

phrases.en: Excuse me, which way is the station?
How far is it from here?

phrases.native: سڌو هلو، پوءِ کاٻي پاسي مڙو.
phrases.roman: sidho halo, poi khāɓe pāse muṛo.

phrases.en: Please turn right at the mosque.
Does this bus go to Hyderabad?

phrases.native: اسين ڪراچيءَ کان ٺٽي تائين ڪار ۾ وياسين.
phrases.roman: asīṃ karāchīa khāṃ ṭhaṭe tāīṃ kāra meṃ vayāsīṃ.
phrases.en: We went by car from Karachi to Thatta.

grammar.title: Giving instructions: the imperative
grammar.body:
Sindhi has three levels of command, matching the levels of 'you':

**Intimate (تون)** — the bare stem: وڃ vañu 'go', اچ achu 'come', ڏس ɗisu 'look', ڪر kar 'do', مڙ muṛu 'turn'.
**Polite (توهان)** — stem + **-o**: وڃو vaño, اچو acho, ڏسو ɗiso, ڪريو karyo, مڙو muṛo.
**Extra-polite / future-request** — stem + **-ijo / -jo**: وڃجو vañijo, اچجو achijo, ڪجو kajo, مڙجو muṛijo — 'please do…', used for gentle requests, advice and instructions to be carried out later.

Irregular: ڏيڻ 'give' → ڏي ɗe / ڏيو ɗiyo; وٺڻ 'take' → وٺ vaṭhu / وٺو vaṭho; کائڻ → کاءُ / کائو; پيئڻ → پيءُ / پيئو.

**Negative**: put **نه** before the verb: نه وڃو 'don't go', فڪر نه ڪريو 'don't worry'. Soften any command with مهرباني ڪري, سائين or ادا.

grammar.title: Movement: ڏانهن 'towards', کان 'from', تائين 'until'
grammar.body:
Postpositions of movement follow the (oblique) noun:

**ڏانهن** ɗāṃhaṃ — towards, to: گهر ڏانهن 'towards home'. With destinations, Sindhi often uses **no postposition at all**: مان ڪراچي وڃان ٿو 'I'm going to Karachi'.
**کان** khāṃ — from (a place or time): ڪراچيءَ کان 'from Karachi', صبح کان 'since morning'.
**مان** māṃ — out of, from inside: گهر مان نڪتو 'came out of the house'.
**تائين** tāīṃ — up to, until, as far as: ٺٽي تائين 'as far as Thatta', شام تائين 'until evening'.
**وٽان** vaṭāṃ — from near, past (a landmark): مسجد وٽان 'at / past the mosque'.

Sides use پاسو 'side' in the oblique: **ساڄي پاسي** 'to the right', **کاٻي پاسي** 'to the left'.

examples.native: هي رستو ڀٽ شاهه ڏانهن وڃي ٿو.
examples.roman: hī rasto bhiṭ shāh ɗāṃhaṃ vañe tho.
examples.en: This road goes to Bhit Shah.
Go straight as far as the crossroads.

examples.native: هو صبح کان ڪم تي آهي.
examples.roman: hū subuha khāṃ kama te āhe.
examples.en: He's been at work since morning.

dialogue.title: Finding Pakka Qila
dialogue.setting: John is in Hyderabad and asks a shopkeeper the way to the old fort, Pakka Qila.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: السلام عليڪم ادا. پڪو قلعو ڪيڏانهن آهي؟
lines.roman: assalāmu ʿalaikum adā. pako qilʿo keɗāṃhaṃ āhe?
lines.en: Hello brother. Which way is Pakka Qila?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: وعليڪم السلام. پنڌ وڃڻ چاهيو ٿا يا رڪشا ۾؟
lines.roman: vaʿalaikum assalām. pandha vañaṇu chāhyo thā yā rikshā meṃ?
lines.en: Hello. Do you want to walk or go by rickshaw?

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: نه، ڏهن منٽن جو پنڌ آهي. هن رستي تي سڌو وڃو.
lines.roman: na, ɗahan minaṭan jo pandhu āhe. hin raste te sidho vaño.
lines.en: No, it's a ten-minute walk. Go straight along this road.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: چوڪ وٽان ساڄي پاسي مڙجو. اتي هڪ وڏي مسجد آهي.
lines.roman: chaunka vaṭāṃ sāʄe pāse muṛijo. ute hika vaɗī masjida āhe.
lines.en: Turn right at the crossroads. There's a big mosque there.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: مسجد جي ڀرسان بازار آهي. بازار جي آخر ۾ قلعو آهي.
lines.roman: masjida jī bharsāṃ bāzāru āhe. bāzāra jī āxira meṃ qilʿo āhe.
lines.en: Next to the mosque is the bazaar. The fort is at the end of the bazaar.

lines.speaker: John
lines.native: سڌو، ساڄي پاسي، پوءِ بازار. مهرباني!
lines.roman: sidho, sāʄe pāse, poi bāzāru. meharbānī!
lines.en: Straight, right, then the bazaar. Thanks!

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: ڪا ڳالهه ناهي. گرمي آهي — پاڻي سان گڏ وٺي وڃجو!
lines.roman: kā ɠālhi nāhe. garmī āhe — pāṇī sāṃ gaɗu vaṭhī vañijo!
lines.en: No problem. It's hot — take water with you!

culture: Hyderabad's **Pakka Qila** (پڪو قلعو, 'the solid fort') was built by the Kalhora and Talpur rulers of Sindh in the 18th century, and the bazaars around it — like the Shahi Bazaar — are among the oldest in Sindh. Rickshaw fares are agreed before you get in. Intercity travel is mostly by road on air-conditioned coaches along the Karachi–Hyderabad motorway and the National Highway; the railway follows the Indus north through Kotri, Nawabshah, Rohri and Sukkur. Women often sit in separate front sections of buses.
